name: Nadab (Jeroboam's son, king of Israel)
title: Second king of the Northern Kingdom of Israel
summary: Nadab was the son of Jeroboam I and the second king over the northern kingdom of Israel. He reigned for only two years before being killed by Baasha in a conspiracy. Nadab continued in his father's sinful ways by maintaining the idolatry that Jeroboam had introduced.

keyEvents.title: Nadab becomes king of Israel
keyEvents.description: After Jeroboam's death, his son Nadab became king over Israel in the second year of Jeroboam's reign as king. He reigned for two years over Israel.

keyEvents.title: Nadab walks in his father's sinful ways
keyEvents.description: Nadab did what was evil in the Lord's sight and walked in the way of his father, in his sin, which he had caused Israel to commit through idolatry.

keyEvents.title: The siege of Gibbethon
keyEvents.description: Nadab and all Israel besieged the Philistine city of Gibbethon. It was during this siege that the conspiracy against him took place.

keyEvents.title: Baasha's Conspiracy and the Murder of Nadab
keyEvents.description: Baasha, son of Ahijah from the tribe of Issachar, conspired against Nadab and struck him down at Gibbethon. Baasha then seized the kingdom in his place.

keyEvents.title: The Destruction of Jeroboam's House
keyEvents.description: When Baasha became king, he killed all the house of Jeroboam. He left not a single soul alive, in fulfillment of the word of the Lord spoken through the prophet Ahijah.

keyEvents.title: Fulfillment of Ahijah's Prophecy
keyEvents.description: The destruction of Jeroboam's lineage by Baasha was the fulfillment of the prophecy that Ahijah from Shiloh had pronounced against Jeroboam because of his sins and idolatry.
